body:
### Feature hasn't been suggested before.

- [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before.

### Describe the enhancement you want to request

### Problem

The current system prompts are heavy and optimized for frontier models.
This causes issues with:
- Smaller local models hitting context limits
- Token waste for simple tasks
- Users who want minimal prompting for specific workflows
- Outdated instructions that don't match current model capabilities (some prompts unchanged for 7+ months)
- Conflicts between default prompts and user's AGENTS.md instructions
- Overspecification that degrades reasoning in high-capability models #10927

### Proposal

Add a system prompt mode setting with initial options:
- Default: current per-model prompts (anthropic.txt, gemini.txt, etc.) — no changes
- Light: minimal prompt with only essential info: tools, basic safety rules, environment

The current proposal covers several things at once:
- Non-breaking: Default behavior unchanged
- Extensible: Opens path for future custom mode where users provide their own prompt
- Addresses multiple issues without requiring prompt rewrites

### Configuration

- Via settings menu (`Ctrl+P` → Settings)
- Via `opencode.json`:
```
{
   "prompt": {
     "mode": "light"
   }
 }
```

### Related issues
- #7101
- #10927
- #11995
- #13605
- #14398

comments.author: m-nelly
comments.body: I'm running a local model with 32k context and it works really well for my use case; however, OpenCode's system prompt is consuming ~10% of that context window. If we could get a configuration option to replace the default system prompt with the agent/model prompt we specify, that would solve this and all of the other related issues.

comments.author: okuyam2y
comments.body:
I opened #32315 before seeing this; it's the same mechanism from the opposite end, so I'll continue here and close mine as a duplicate.

This issue frames the switcher around a `Light` mode for small/local models. The same opt-in selector also solves the high-capability end — and #10927 (overspecification degrading reasoning in capable models), which is cited above, is exactly the case I have data for.

I prototyped a `Frontier` mode (the same idea as `Light`, just a different target): a prompt variant that pushes GPT/Claude-class models toward root-cause reasoning instead of "looks fine" conclusions. Measured with a within-session controlled A/B on a public code-review task (planetiler, last 10 commits, known seeded regressions) — same model, same agent prompt, same session, only the system prompt swapped:

| bug (public-API silent semantic change) | baseline | frontier |
|---|:-:|:-:|

comments.author: thekk1
comments.body: This would be a very welcome improvement for our local infrastrukture.

comments.author: violog
comments.body: My issue https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/39537 is a duplicate of this. I would like a config option to disable/replace system prompt in particular. Don't see any reason for prompts to be built-in, since Opencode is an open and highly customizable tools, in contrary to competitors.

comments.author: justauserid
comments.body:
Why not just let the user nuke everything from a certain agent session? Offering this `OPENCODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_CODE` only as a global setting sort of diminishes this flag's capability.

There is a good chance a user might want all the circus and drama Calude Code has to offer on the same machine, esp. if it's a complex task (says a complex coding project or huge codebase, or both). But say another user (or the same user) at some point wants to just work with a few .txt/.md files in a directory and needs writing feedback, or so, it's absolutely bonkers in that case that OpenCode would still send something like git or node or whatever, unless the user completely shut that off via that flag.

I see issues closer to that have been closed before #1157 #5637

title: [FEATURE]: System prompt mode switcher (Default/Light)
